summary: Chinese has two everyday negators, placed directly before the verb (or before a place phrase with 在). 不 (bù) negates habits, likes, wishes, decisions, the present and the future, adjectives and 是. 没 (méi, often 没有) negates 有 and says that something did not happen or has not happened yet. There is no ‘do’ and no change of the verb.

head: Meaning
Negator
Example
rows: 我不喜欢洋葱。 I don’t like onions.
这不是西红柿。 This isn’t a tomato.
黄瓜不在这里。 The cucumber isn’t here.
我没有南瓜。 I don’t have a pumpkin.
他没吃茄子。 He didn’t eat the eggplant.

blocks.title: bù or bú?
blocks.text: 不 is said bú before a 4th tone: 不是 bú shì, 不要 bú yào, 不在 bú zài; bù elsewhere: 不喜欢 bù xǐhuan.

items.title: 不 — will, habit, state
points: 他不吃茄子。 He doesn’t eat eggplant (never does / won’t).
Also with 是, 在 and adjectives.

items.title: 没 — fact, event
points: 他没吃茄子。 He didn’t eat the eggplant (it didn’t happen).

askYourself: Is the verb 有 (have / there is)? → 没有 — never 不有.
Is the verb 是 (is)? → 不是 — never 没是.
Am I saying that something did not happen, or has not happened yet? → 没 + verb, without 了.
Is it a habit, a preference, a wish, a decision or the future? → 不 + verb.
Is the syllable after 不 in the 4th tone? → say bú.
steps: Find the verb (or the 在 + place phrase).
Choose 不 or 没 with the questions above.
Put the negator directly in front of it; nothing else changes.
With 没有, drop 一 + measure word: 我有一个南瓜 → 我没有南瓜.

traps: *我不有南瓜 → 我没有南瓜.
*他没是老师 → 他不是老师.
*我没吃了 → 我没吃 (没 and 了 do not go together here).
不要 + verb is the command ‘don’t!’; ‘I don’t want to eat’ is 我不想吃.
Under 没有, 一个 normally disappears: 我没有南瓜, not 我没有一个南瓜.
